scope: prove or disprove the ring-B delivery hypothesis by disabling the snapshot filter

root_cause_candidate_confirmed_in_code.filter: if (not data.startswith(b'\xff\xff\xff\xff') and not fragment and state_now < args.reliable_until_state): drop as 'drop_snapshot'
root_cause_candidate_confirmed_in_code.meaning: with the default of 9, every non-fragment server packet is discarded while the client phase is below 9; our sessions sit at phase 5, so NONE of our 206-byte replies were ever written into ring B

experiment.change: ran forward with --reliable-until-state 0 to disable the snapshot filter
experiment.result: client messageAck still 1, acked_our_seq still false, while our seq 6/7 206-byte replies were emitted

interpretation.filter_was_a_real_blocker: the code path proves our earlier replies were dropped before injection, which invalidates the earlier 'body is wrong' reasoning
interpretation.filter_off_did_not_fix_it: with the filter off the client still does not acknowledge, so a second issue exists downstream
remaining_candidates: the 206-byte all-zero body is not a valid service message and is discarded by the client before it forms an ack
inject_oob_raw writes an adr stub with type/ip/port that the client's receive path rejects
the client only acknowledges packets carrying a netchan fragment/reliable command (FRAGMENT_BIT), which our replies never set

next: log forward's injected counter explicitly (it is only emitted in the final record, which a kill loses) so delivery into ring B can be proven per packet
